definition: Distributed attention is a proposed style of attention in meditation, contrasted with focused attention, in which awareness is spread more broadly rather than concentrated on a single target. In the source, some practices such as Vipassana and Rig-pa were described as using distributed attention, although the article notes that this focused-versus-distributed classification has not received strong empirical support.

reasons: The packet does not define “distributed attention” as awareness “spread more broadly rather than concentrated on a single target.” It only references attempts to categorize meditation as using “focused or distributed attentional systems” without describing this broad-vs-single-target characterization.

The packet supports that focused vs distributed attention is a proposed classification, that it includes examples (Shamatha vs Vipassana; and Rig-pa vs Deity), and that the focused-versus-distributed dichotomy “received strong empirical support” (i.e., lacked strong empirical support), but the first sentence includes an unsupported explanatory description of the term.

The packet supports a focused-versus-distributed attentional classification in meditation and says this dichotomy lacks strong empirical support, but it does not define distributed attention as awareness being spread broadly or as the opposite of concentrating on a single target.

The packet identifies Vipassana and Rig-pa as practices thought to use distributed attention, but the definition goes beyond the source by presenting that interpretation as the sense of the term rather than as the article’s tentative classification.
